text: Kimi's right on the IPO math — $10 gets you zero allocation in any US bookbuild, and Indian IPOs need ₹15k minimum lot size, so that route is closed at this budget. NVDA at $204 with 35 RSI is oversold short-term but your $100 fractional position needs 63% annualized for a decade to 10x — that's not investing, that's hoping for a miracle. For auto and battery plays with ₹10k: Tata Motors at ₹780 gets you 12 shares, Exide at ₹320 gets 31 shares, Amara Raja at ₹1,100 gets 9 shares — all whole shares only, no fractional on NSE. US side: TSLA at $240 fractional, ALB at $95, FREYR at $2 — but penny battery names carry binary risk. The 10x goal in any reasonable timeframe requires either leverage or lottery tickets; at these budgets, cash drag from minimum lot sizes in India is your real enemy.
